t: #2575 Find the Divisibility Array of a String
o: For each prefix of a digit string we must report whether its numeric value divides evenly by m (m up to 10⁹, length up to 10⁵). Converting each prefix to an integer is O(n²) and overflows 64 bits, so we carry only the remainder: value(prefix[0..i]) mod m = (previous remainder · 10 + digit) mod m. Example 2: remainders of "1010" mod 10 are 1,0,1,0 → flags 0,1,0,1.
k: Only the remainder mod m matters — never build the full number.
The recurrence rem = (rem·10 + d) % m processes the string in one pass.

a.i: Maintain the remainder of the current prefix modulo m. Appending digit d multiplies the value by 10 and adds d, so the new remainder follows the recurrence above; flag 1 exactly when it hits 0.
s: For each character: rem = (rem·10 + digit) % m; append 1 if rem == 0 else 0.

w: This is the canonical 'big number mod small number' idiom worth memorizing. Pitfall: in C++/Java use a 64-bit intermediate since rem·10 + 9 can exceed 32-bit range only if m is large — rem < m ≤ 10⁹ so rem·10 fits in 64 bits. Follow-up: return prefixes divisible by m² (same idea, larger modulus).
